title: Survey on the international significance of the sense of smell across multiple age groups
summary:
This study investigates how important the sense of smell is for people of different age groups in various countries. The sense of smell plays an important role in everyday life, for example in detecting dangers, enjoying food, and social interactions. However, little is known about whether the importance of smell changes over the course of life and whether there are cultural differences between countries.

For this purpose, a previously developed and validated questionnaire will be translated into several languages and completed by children, adults, and older individuals in their respective home countries. Participation is voluntary, anonymous, and without any risks, as it only involves completing a questionnaire. The results will help to better understand international and age-related differences in the importance of the sense of smell.

interventions.name:
Participants from different countries fill out the questionnaire.
There are three age groups: 10-12 years, 20-30 years, and over 60 years.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age by group:

10–12 years

20–30 years

Over 60 years
Exclusion criteria:
Major underlying diseases:
Diabetes mellitus
Kidney disease
Epilepsy

Acute allergies with allergic rhinitis

Known olfactory disorders

Cognitive impairments, especially regarding language comprehension

Anosmia or hyposmia (complete or partial loss of smell)
